title: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 (rotary/rope fused ops) + KV continuous batching & scheduler improvements
author: Asha Ramesh
release_notes: Improves attention kernel performance by migrating to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/ROPE ops and introduces continuous KV batching + scheduler heuristics. Expected latency reduction ~20-35% on 8k-context workloads and ~15-25% cost savings in steady-state for typical conversational workloads.
description:
Motivation: We observed tail latency and throughput regressions on long-context workloads and expensive per-token kernel launches when using the legacy attention path. This PR migrates our GPU attention path to FlashAttentionV2, adds fused rotary/ROPE support, and integrates fused ops to reduce kernel overhead. In parallel, we improve the KV path with continuous batching and scheduler heuristics to better pack KV cache workload across concurrent requests.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a FlashAttentionV2-backed attention kernel with optional fused rotary/ROPE math paths.
- Adds fused query/key/value interleaving and fused output linear + dropout where supported.
- Implements a continuous KV batching layer that aggregates KV updates across small requests and emits larger batched kernel calls.
- Updates the scheduler to prefer packing short-prefill requests into pending KV batches and adds cost-based gating to trade latency vs throughput.
- Adds unit + integration tests and new perf benchmarks covering 2k/8k/32k context lengths.

Checklist: [x] kernel implementation and ops registration
[x] CPU fallbacks for non-CUDA environments
[x] integration with existing model packing and compilation paths
[x] perf harness and regression asserts
[x] docs/notes for operators and runtime flags

Related: Linear ENG-3421 (attention kernel revamp), ENG-3499 (KV batching), SUP-1281 (customer report: high tail latency on long-context chat). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/flashattnv2-migration and internal notes in docs/notes/flashattnv2-migration.md.

Implementation notes: The FlashAttentionV2 implementation is placed behind a runtime feature flag (runtime.attn.v2_enabled) and a per-model opt-in (model_config.attention_impl = "flashattnv2"). We keep the original kernel registered as a fallback. The fused rotary/ROPE path is guarded by model rotary encoding metadata; we fall back to separate rotary application when unavailable. Continuous KV batching lives in the scheduler component and exposes two knobs: max_batch_time_ms and max_kv_batch_size.

Compatibility: No API surface changes. Customers using pinning by kernel should be aware of the opt-in flag. No breaking changes expected.

Benchmarks (see perf_summary below) show consistent improvements across MPT-30B and Llama-2 13B family on A100 and H100 instances.

review_comments: Diego Ortega (2026-02-19): Please add a fallback path for non-CUDA envs and ensure we don't regress memory for small-batch realtime traffic. Action: added CPU fallback and added microbench that tests 1-4 batch sizes. -- Asha

Marta Liu (2026-02-20): The fused rotary path looks good but please add a numerical equivalence test (float16) vs the existing implementation. Action: added equivalence tests at 1e-3 tolerance and CI perf check. -- Asha

Liam Chen (2026-02-22): Scheduler heuristics look promising; one concern is starvation of long-running prefills. Suggest adding a soft quota per-model for KV batch consumption. Action: added per-model kv_batch_quota and a conservative default. -- Asha
Diego Ortega (2026-02-23): CI flake on perf harness observed (OOM on 32k run). Resolved by lowering internal scratch allocation and adding a retry. -- Asha
perf_summary: Summary: On A100 (40GB) using Llama-2 13B, 8k context: end-to-end median token latency reduced from 86ms -> 58ms (~32%); throughput (tokens/sec) improved by ~28% under steady-state. On H100 with MPT-30B, 32k context prefill: attention kernel time reduced by 35-40% and KV memory traffic reduced by ~18% due to fused ops and larger KV batches. Continuous KV batching increased GPU utilization by ~12% for mixed small/short chat workloads, with tail latency (p95) unchanged for high-priority routes due to scheduler gating. Regression asserts in perf harness: no increase in token-level error for fused rotary vs baseline within tolerance. Detailed CSVs in perf artifacts attached to CI run.
notes: Rollout plan: feature-flag controlled; canary on dedicated pools for 48h with telemetry watching p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and GPU memory. If regressions >5% on p95 for canary, auto-disable. Also tagged for QA smoke on Private deployments due to different CUDA runtimes.
changelog_entry: Upgrade: Attention kernels -> FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/ROPE and continuous KV batching. Performance and bookkeeping improvements for long-context workloads (see release notes).
